amendments.why: Rule 15's supplied-determiner clauses, read as they stand, reach any word standing before a noun that carries no determiner morpheme, and they explicitly forbid marking such a word `added`. That wording covers the ASV's partitive any of the fugitives (JDG.12.5) and one of the cities (JDG.12.7), where folding the quantifier into the construct noun's unit would put two English words no morpheme licenses inside a noun's rendering — and would have to swallow a supplied *of* as well, which no sentence of the rule places. The distinguishing fact is mechanical and already in the rule's own idiom of counting determiners: the ASV writes its own supplied *the* immediately before the noun's word, so the quantifier occupies no determiner slot. The amendment states that boundary and defers, as the rule already does elsewhere, to a present מִן (rule 19's מִן־הַבָּשָׂר → any of the flesh), a present כֹּל, or a numeral standing in the phrase (rule 15's own לְאֶחָד מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת → unto one of the family), so nothing in the corpus rows or in the contract is contradicted; only the case none of them covers is decided.
amendments.rule: The article `הַ` aligns to English *the*. Hebrew has no indefinite article, so an English *a* or *an* belongs to the noun that licenses it and is not `added`. **The same ownership applies to a definite article the ASV supplies where no Hebrew article morpheme is present:** it belongs to the nominal expression it determines and is not `added`. **Read that as the noun of the expression, not as its leftmost word.** Where the expression writes both a numeral and the noun it counts, the supplied determiner joins that noun's unit and the numeral takes only its own word: `בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר יוֹם` → *the fifteenth day* gives *the day* to `יוֹם` and *fifteenth* to the numeral, and `לִשְׁלֹשָׁה עָשָׂר פָּרִים` → *of the thirteen bullocks* and `לְאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר כְּבָשִׂים` → *of the fourteen lambs* give *the bullocks* and *the lambs* to their nouns. A numeral takes such a determiner only where the Hebrew writes no noun for it to determine, which is rule 31's substantival numeral — `בְּאֶחָד לַחֹדֶשׁ` → *on* ***the first day*** *of the month*. And this reaches a supplied determiner only: where an article morpheme stands in the phrase it takes the written *the* first, under rules 29 and 47, and where the ASV writes a distributive *each* or *every* the numeral takes that word under rule 41. **And it applies to a supplied quantifying determiner such as *any*, which is the word English writes in that same slot where *a* will not stand — under a negation, in a question, or after a comparative.** Where a bare noun carries no determiner morpheme of its own and the ASV writes an *any* before it, that word determines the nominal expression exactly as a supplied *a* or *the* does: it joins the noun's unit, is not `added`, and is never the head, which stays on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31 — `לִמְלָאכָה` → *for any work* gives *for* to the preposition and *any work* to the noun, headed on *work*. **But only where no morpheme in the clause licenses that determiner.** A `כֹּל` standing on the noun is itself what the *any* renders and takes it, the noun keeping only its own word — `כָּל־עֵץ` → *any tree*, `כָּל־כְּלִי` → *any vessel* — and where the ASV recasts a clause's negation onto a nominal standing in it, the negative takes the determiner that negation has become. **Read which nominal the ASV has put the determiner on rather than what its grammatical role is**: an object takes it in `לֹא יֵעָשֶׂה לִמְלָאכָה` → *it was meet for* ***no*** *work*, which gives *no* to `לֹא`, discontinuous from the verb it negates under rule 25, and leaves `מְלָאכָה` the bare *work*; a subject takes it in `אַל־תָּבֹא רְנָנָה בוֹ` → *Let* ***no*** *joyful voice come therein*, which gives *no* to `אַל` and leaves the noun its own *joyful voice*. A jussive or prohibitive `אַל` is read on the same terms as `לֹא`. Count the determiners and read which morpheme each answers to, as rule 41 counts a phrase's determiners and rule 29 counts its *the*s. This does not reach a supplied possessive, which rule 18 leaves `added` where no suffix or other possessive morpheme is present. **A supplied determiner that distinguishes one member of a class from another is read on exactly those terms.** Where the ASV writes a correlative *one … another*, or another contrastive determiner standing where an *a* or a *the* would stand, before a noun that carries no determiner morpheme of its own, that word determines the nominal expression as a supplied *a* or *any* does: it joins the noun's unit, is not `added`, and is never the head. `מִמַּטֶּה לְמַטֶּה אַחֵר` → *from* ***one*** *tribe to another tribe* gives *one tribe* to the first `מַטֶּה`, headed on *tribe*, while `אַחֵר` keeps the *another* written for it. Do not read such a word as evidence that a numeral stands in the phrase, and do not mark it `added` under rule 30 because it is not one of the determiners named above: what decides it is that no morpheme in the phrase licenses the word, which is the count the preceding sentences run. But run that count first, since a numeral standing in the phrase is itself what such a word renders and takes it under rule 31 — `לְאֶחָד מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת` → *unto* ***one*** *of the family* — and one chapter may write both shapes, as NUM.36.8 and NUM.36.9 do. **But a quantifier the ASV writes before a determiner of its own is standing in no determiner's slot at all.** Every supplied determiner above stands where an *a* or a *the* would stand before the noun's own word. Where the ASV instead writes a partitive expression — a quantifier and an *of* before a nominal that already carries a written or a supplied *the* of its own, as *any of the fugitives* or *one of the cities* — the quantifier heads a phrase of its own and determines nothing, so the sentences above do not reach it: where no morpheme in the clause licenses the expression, the quantifier and its *of* stand together and do one office, and they are one `added` unit under rule 2, headed on the quantifier. Read which determiner stands immediately before the noun's own word, as rule 29 counts the ASV's *the*s; a noun holding a *the* of its own is not a noun the quantifier determines, and an *of* the ASV writes between the two nouns of a construct chain is the rectum's under rule 19 whatever partitive stands before the chain. But run that count first as well, since a morpheme standing in the clause takes the expression before this sentence reaches it: a partitive `מִן` takes *any of* whole under rule 19, a `כֹּל` standing on the noun takes the *any* under this rule's earlier sentences, and a numeral standing in the phrase takes the *one* under rule 31, as `לְאֶחָד מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת` → *unto* ***one*** *of the family* does above. Where nothing does, `פְּלִיטֵי אֶפְרַיִם` → ***any of*** *the fugitives of Ephraim* and `בְּעָרֵי גִלְעָד` → *in* ***one of*** *the cities of Gilead* leave both supplied words `added`, the construct noun keeping the supplied *the* rule 29 gives it and the rectum its own *of*. An ASV italic on such a pair corroborates it and decides nothing, by rule 7. **For Aramaic, a separately segmented determined-state ending (`Td`) is treated likewise:** align it to *the* when the ASV writes a corresponding article, and mark it `unrepresented` under rule 29 when the ASV writes no separate article, including where another determiner supplies the determination. **A determiner that directly realizes another morpheme is not a corresponding article.** In the temporal relative `עִדָּנָא דִּי` → *what time*, *what* realizes the written relative `דִּי`, while the determined-state ending is `unrepresented`; the relative morpheme takes the word before the nominal determination does, exactly as a present `כֹּל` or negative takes its determiner above. More specific construct and substantival rules still decide which source unit inside that expression takes it.

conventions: An italic partitive the ASV supplies before a definite construct chain — any of the fugitives of Ephraim (v5), one of the cities of Gilead (v7) — answers to no morpheme in this chapter: no מִן, כֹּל or numeral stands in either clause, and the chain's own of belongs to the rectum under rule 19. The quantifier and its of are one added unit headed on the quantifier, while the construct noun keeps the supplied the rule 29 gives it. Do not read the quantifier as a supplied determiner under rule 15: the ASV writes its own the after it, so it determines nothing.

MACULA segments the toponym בֵּית לֶחֶם as two Np tokens sharing one lemma. The ASV writes Beth lehem in two words, so each token takes the word written for it and neither is fused or left unrepresented (rule 2). JDG.12.8 and JDG.12.10 are aligned alike.

report: Read all 23 candidate groups and the full dump end to end, including the added units the lemma table is blind to. No construction is analysed two ways with nothing in the source to license the difference, so patches is empty.

Multi-treatment buckets are all ASV-driven. פָּלִיט is a verbless predicate taking the construction-supplied copula at v4 (rule 20) and a construct noun taking a supplied the at v5 (rule 29). גִּלְעָד and אֶפְרַיִם appear as bare names, as of-recta, and as gentilic plurals with a supplied determiner joining the name's unit (rule 15). The dative לְ takes unto at v5 and v6 but is unrepresented at v9 and v14, where the had recasting leaves it nothing (rules 40, 43). Every waw takes the connective the ASV wrote and is unrepresented where it wrote none.

Checked the added units the table cannot see. The italic partitives any* of* (v5) and one* of* (v7) are handled identically: one added unit each, headed on the quantifier, with the construct noun keeping its supplied the (rule 29) and the rectum its own of (rule 19). Supplied object pronouns are added at v3 and v6; the supplied coordinator between the two midst phrases is added at v4; phrasal particles completing a source lexeme (together, over, up, in) stay with their verbs at v1, v3, v4, v5 and v9.

Cross-checked the recurring frames against one another: the two הָיָה־לוֹ possessive clauses (v9, v14), the four Niphal was buried units (v7, v10, v12, v15), the two demonstrative phrases whose single written determiner goes to the pronoun and leaves both articles unrepresented (v3 this day, v6 that time), the two identical fords of the Jordan chains (v5, v6), and the three after him units (v8, v11, v13). All agree.

BSB: none of the thirteen disagreements is a genuine error. They are the documented convention differences — unrendered waws, the object marker, the two cohortative he tokens at v3 (rule 32 names this divergence), assimilated and agreement articles, and the possessive לְ silenced by the had recasting (rule 21 names this case itself). Nothing was changed to improve the rate.

One amendment returned, to rule 15. Read as it stands, its supplied-determiner clauses would fold one of and any of into the noun's unit; but the ASV writes its own supplied the after the quantifier there, so the quantifier stands in no determiner slot and heads a partitive phrase instead. The amendment marks that boundary and defers to a present מִן, כֹּל or numeral, so it leaves rule 19's מִן־הַבָּשָׂר → any of the flesh and rule 15's own לְאֶחָד מִמִּשְׁפַּחַת untouched.
